title: Protect bright highlights
tip: Check the brightest part of the scene and lower the exposure if important detail is becoming completely white.

title: Change one setting at a time
tip: When learning manual controls, adjust aperture, shutter speed, or ISO individually so you can see exactly how each setting changes the photograph.

title: Check the background
tip: Before taking a photograph, look around the edges of the frame for distracting objects.

title: Move before you zoom
tip: Try stepping left, right, closer, or lower to improve the relationships between the subject and background before using digital zoom.

title: Turn the subject toward the light
tip: For a simple portrait, position the subject near a window and slowly turn them until the light shapes the face clearly.

title: Use open shade at midday
tip: Move a person into the shade of a building or tree to avoid harsh overhead shadows while keeping the light bright and even.

title: Choose one dominant colour
tip: A scene often feels more organised when one colour leads and other colours act as smaller supporting accents.

title: Check white balance indoors
tip: If an indoor photograph looks strongly orange, blue, or green, try a white-balance preset that matches the main light source.

title: Create a steady stance
tip: Keep your elbows close to your body, hold the camera with both hands, and gently press the shutter instead of jabbing it.

title: Support slow exposures
tip: When using a slow shutter speed, place the camera on a tripod or stable surface and use a short timer to reduce camera shake.

title: Focus on the nearest eye
tip: For a portrait with shallow depth of field, place the focus point on the eye closest to the camera.

title: Give the subject direction
tip: Ask the person to make a small action, such as looking toward the light or adjusting a sleeve, to create a more natural expression and pose.
